findings.message: The commit changes code under plugins/specclaw-fleet (lib/, pipelines/, k8s/, skills/) but the diff bumps no version. No plugin.json (.claude-plugin or .codex-plugin) and no entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json is touched. The new default image tag 0.8.9 is also tied to a plugin version that does not change here. Bump every plugin.json and every marketplace.json plugins[] entry to the same new version.
findings.scenario: The PR changes plugins/specclaw-fleet/lib/trigger.sh, dispatch.sh and launch.sh. All manifests stay at their old version. Installed users never see an update, and the pinned image tag ghcr.io/chan4lk/specclaw-fleet:0.8.9 no longer matches any released plugin version.

findings.message: The FLEET_REF fix (a B1 major) ships a single variant row: refs/heads/feature/fleet-x. Missing rows are refs/heads/main, an already-bare 'main', unset or empty, and a non-branch ref such as refs/tags/x or refs/pull/1/merge. The test extracts the step only from pipelines/dispatch.yml (tests/lib/pipeline-env.sh), so the identical edit in pipelines/dispatch-hosted.yml has no test. The two copies can drift. Make the test table-driven over these variants and run it against both templates.
findings.scenario: Someone changes only the hosted template back to ${FLEET_REF##*/}, or drops the unset-guard there. Every test stays green, and hosted runs clone 'fleet-x' instead of 'feature/fleet-x'.

findings.message: F_COMMIT and F_REPO now come from FLEET_DISPATCH_COMMIT and FLEET_REPO_URL, taken from the environment with no validation. The other inputs are validated (FLEET_IMAGE, FLEET_NAMESPACE, F_REF). Plain `specclaw-fleet dispatch` honours these variables too, so the approval gate can be checked against the local tree while a different commit or repo is dispatched. Only trigger should set these. Validate the commit as ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ and the URL as an expected https form, or pass them as explicit internal arguments instead of ambient env vars.
findings.scenario: A stale FLEET_DISPATCH_COMMIT=deadbeef… or FLEET_REPO_URL=https://evil/x.git is exported in the shell or CI variables. `specclaw-fleet dispatch 049-x` checks approval locally, then launches a Job that clones the wrong repo or commit. The run record shows the injected values as the dispatched commit.

findings.message: The default image reference ghcr.io/chan4lk/specclaw-fleet:0.8.9 is hard-coded in lib/dispatch.sh, in pipelines/dispatch.yml (fleetImage), and in the ac5 test. These copies must be bumped together on every release. If dispatch-hosted.yml carries its own default, it is a fourth copy that this commit did not touch. Keep one source (for example, derive the tag from the plugin version) and have the other places read it.
findings.scenario: The next release bumps the pipeline variable to 0.9.0 but not the lib default. A local `specclaw-fleet dispatch` runs the old 0.8.9 image while pipeline runs use 0.9.0, so the same change gets different agent and plugin code depending on how it was dispatched.

findings.message: FLEET_REF now takes $(Build.SourceBranch) and strips only refs/heads/. A tag or PR run (refs/tags/v1, refs/pull/12/merge) passes through unstripped and still satisfies dispatch's ref regex. It is then used as a branch name. Fail closed on any value that does not start with refs/heads/. Apply the same change to dispatch-hosted.yml.
findings.scenario: The pipeline is run from a tag or PR ref. FLEET_REF=refs/pull/12/merge is accepted as a 'branch', and the pod clones a nonexistent branch or the wrong thing.
